Latigo Biotherapeutics, Clinical-Stage Developer of Selective Nav1.8 Non‑Opioid Pain Medicines for Acute and Chronic Pain, Files for Nasdaq Global Select Market IPO
data.description:
Latigo Biotherapeutics, a clinical-stage developer of non-opioid pain medicines, priced its IPO at $18.00 per share and will list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol LTGO. The company sold 19,200,000 shares, for gross proceeds of approximately $345.6 million, with an additional 2,880,000 shares available to underwriters via an option. Net proceeds are earmarked to advance late-stage trials for its lead Nav1.8 inhibitor LTG-001 and to progress its chronic pain candidate LTG-321.

Business Description

Latigo Biotherapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing non‑opioid pain medicines that work by selectively inhibiting Nav1.8, a sodium channel central to peripheral pain signaling. Its lead candidate, LTG‑001, is an oral (with IV in development) therapy for moderate to severe acute pain designed to deliver rapid analgesia and reduce opioid use. In a 343‑patient abdominoplasty study, LTG‑001 met the primary endpoint (SPID48), showed faster onset versus an opioid comparator, and demonstrated opioid‑sparing. The company plans a Phase 3 bunionectomy trial and an open‑label safety study with topline results expected in the second half of 2027, targeting an NDA thereafter.

Latigo’s second program, LTG‑321, is a next‑generation Nav1.8 inhibitor for chronic musculoskeletal pain starting with osteoarthritis of the knee. Phase 1 results showed dose-proportional PK and robust pharmacodynamic activity in the cold pressor test with once-daily potential; a Phase 2 proof‑of‑concept trial in OA is underway with topline results anticipated in the second half of 2027. An early program, LTG‑418, aims to enable lower-dose formulations and alternative routes (e.g., gels, patches, eye drops, inhalers, injectables), expanding the company’s reach in pain management.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Pain drives an estimated 250 million prescriptions annually in the U.S.
  • Market growth: Rising demand tied to aging demographics and shift away from opioids.
  • Market position: Focused on selective Nav1.8 inhibition with multiple shots on goal across acute and chronic musculoskeletal pain.
  • Key competitors: Vertex (suzetrigine/Journavx), AbbVie, Eli Lilly (SiteOne), Grünenthal, Merck; emerging players in Nav1.7 and Kv7 channels.
  • Industry trends: Transition to non-opioid, peripherally acting analgesics; regulatory precedent set by 2025 suzetrigine approval; emphasis on opioid-sparing outcomes.

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Pre-commercial; no product revenue to date
  • Locations: Headquarters in Thousand Oaks, CA; additional office in South San Francisco, CA
  • Geographic presence: United States-focused clinical development
  • Partnerships: Exclusive license with the Lieber Institute covering Nav1.8 IP
  • Orders/GMV: Not applicable (biopharma R&D stage)
  • Other key metrics: 59 full-time employees as of March 31, 2026; FDA Fast Track Designation for LTG-001 (Feb 18, 2025); Abdominoplasty Phase 2 study enrolled 343 patients; Planned Phase 3 bunionectomy trial ~400 patients; OA Phase 2 trial ~120 patients

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): No revenue to date
  • Revenue growth: Not applicable
  • Operating income: Operating expenses of $110.4 million in 2025
  • Net income: Net loss of $109.2 million in 2025; net loss of $61.2 million in 2024

Management

  • Nima Farzan, President and Chief Executive Officer - Former CEO of Kinnate Biopharma and PaxVax; earlier roles at Novartis; led IPO and M&A transactions.
  • Neil Singla, M.D., Chief Medical Officer - Pain trial expert; founder of Lotus Clinical Research; led/participated in 250+ pain studies and 75+ FDA interactions.
  • Neha Krishnamohan, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Business Officer - Former CFO of Artiva and Kinnate; 15+ years in healthcare investment banking at Goldman Sachs.
  • Timothy P. Walbert, Chair of the Board - Former Chairman/CEO of Horizon Therapeutics; senior advisor to Amgen; extensive public-company leadership.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: Latigo Biotherapeutics, Inc.
  • Filing date: August 07, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: LTGO
  • Exchange: Nasdaq Global Select Market
  • Price range: $18.00 per share
  • Offering size: $345,600,000 gross proceeds
  • Shares offered: 19,200,000 shares (underwriters’ option for 2,880,000 additional shares)
  • Lead underwriters: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC; Jefferies; Leerink Partners; Guggenheim Securities
  • Use of proceeds: Fund Phase 3 bunionectomy and open-label safety trials and NDA submission for LTG-001 and commercial readiness; advance LTG-321 through Phase 2 OA proof-of-concept and start Phase 3; support LTG-418 and other R&D working capital and general corporate purposes.

Original SEC Filing: Latigo Biotherapeutics, Inc. - 424B4 - Aug. 07, 2026

data.description:

  • Revenue: $3,000 for Q2 2026, down from $7,000 in the year-ago quarter ( (57%) YoY).

  • Revenue mix and channels: Biotech retail sales fell 57% quarter-over-quarter for Q2 2026 but are up 43% year-to-date versus 2025, reflecting early traction for the Celios product line acquired in February 2025. Sales are now primarily through online and third-party distributors.

  • Cost discipline: SG&A, professional fees and other operating costs were materially reduced. R&D spending has been paused or re-targeted to prioritize monetizable intellectual property.
